Awaiting essential project information to begin planning work. Cannot proceed with plan development without project ID, task description, scope definition, and resource/timeline constraints.
No project information was provided in the handoff from the Planner. Cannot initialize implementation work without a project ID, task description, and scope definition.

The Implementer correctly identified that no project information was provided in the handoff from the Planner, making it impossible to initialize implementation work. No implementation work was attempted, and no deliverables were produced. The root cause is a failure in the Planner's handoff to provide essential project details (project ID, task description, scope definition). Downstream review cannot proceed without this foundational information being established.

The Implementer correctly identified and escalated the absence of project information (project ID, task description, scope) from the Planner's handoff. Rather than proceeding with assumptions or fabricated details, the Implementer appropriately halted work pending essential project context. This is the correct response to an upstream failure. The implementation work itself cannot be faulted—no implementation was possible without foundational project details.

Testing halted due to upstream failure. The Implementer appropriately identified and escalated the absence of critical project information (project ID, task description, scope). No implementation work was performed, making it impossible to verify requirements compliance. This escalation was the correct response, but it leaves no implementation artifact for the Tester to evaluate. Further testing is blocked pending proper project handoff from the Planner.
